A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BadRDM work, and all 11 pages of each are readable. However, both end with references without supplying the cited appendices, limiting comparison of supplementary settings, analyses, and material redirected there in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack and generation-quality measurements, variant and hyperparameter ablations, natural-trigger examples, and defense evaluations in Tables 1–2 and Figures 3–6.

after.justification: v2 reports original attack comparisons, variant ablations, generation examples, and defense evaluations, including external-baseline results in Table 1.

M1.justification: The poisoning and utility losses, text-encoder-only fine-tuning, entropy selection, and generative augmentation remain the same. Explicit prompt conditioning in v2 clarifies inputs already specified in v1 Section 4.1 rather than establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain class-conditional and text-to-image generation using CC3M, ImageNet, Open Images, and MS-COCO. v2 still states that natural-text triggers were explored, referring to Appendix C.3; the missing main-text examples therefore do not establish removal of that scenario.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds PoiMM, BadT2I, and BadCM comparisons for both tasks, substantially extending v1's comparisons against No Attack and BadRDM variants. The variants and BFT/CleanCLIP defenses remain elsewhere. The comparator labeled BadT2I is linked to reference 49, Rickrolling the Artist.

E3.justification: The shared experiments retain the stated training budgets, retrieval count, evaluation metrics, and sample counts. v2 newly refers to an image-only conditioning evaluation in Appendix C, but that appendix is unavailable in both PDFs, preventing determination of whether this introduces a protocol or merely documents an existing test.

E4.justification: The variant ablations, Figure 5 sensitivity studies, and defense evaluations match after relocation and renumbering. However, v1's natural-trigger study in Section 4.4/Figure 6 is redirected to unavailable Appendix C.3 in v2. Its retention or revision, and changes to other referenced supplementary analyses, cannot be verified.

E5.justification: The supplied tables and figures continue to report point estimates and averages over attack targets without seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new comparator results do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 Table 1 adds PoiMM/BadT2I/BadCM ASRs of 0.6069/0.6205/0.5412 for class-conditional generation and 0.6738/0.5189/0.6892 for T2I, alongside other metrics. BadRDM remains at 0.9089/0.9643 ASR, and the original ablation and defense values are retained. The new table gives class-conditional No Attack FID as 20.7495, whereas v1 and v2 Table 2 give 20.7459.

T1.justification: Equation (1) adds q as a direct conditioning variable alongside retrieved neighbors, correcting the formal transition distribution to match the input setup already stated in v1 Section 4.1. The losses, selection equation, and threat assumptions otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal introduction/conclusion claims remain: the first investigation of RDM backdoors, contactless retrieval poisoning, two surrogate-enhancement strategies, and effective attacks with preserved benign utility. The additional baseline evidence supports these retained claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 attributes baseline failures to unreliable retrieval of accurate, high-quality surrogates. Section 4.3 also argues that the existing variants outperforming external baselines supports contrastive poisoning even without TSE. These interpretations extend v1's discussion of comparisons among its own variants.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 newly states the default set size |v_s| = 4, without establishing that an experimental setting changed. v2 also references pseudocode and baseline adaptation details in Appendices A and B.4, but those missing sections cannot be credited as available implementation documentation.

R1.justification: v2 adds PHANTOM, AgentPoison, a trustworthy-RAG survey, and citations supporting the new multimodal baselines, while removing peripheral GAN and inversion references. Section 2.2 more explicitly positions RDM attacks relative to existing RAG-LLM poisoning research; the central novelty claim remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Prose is tightened across the introduction, related work, and method sections. The variant discussion moves from Section 4.2 to 4.3, and the natural-trigger section becomes an appendix reference. Kuofeng Gao is added to the author list, while the overall document structure remains similar.

P2.justification: v2 adds the external-baseline Table 1, relocates the original comparison as Table 2, and renumbers the defense table to Table 3. Figure 6 is no longer displayed in the supplied PDF. Figures 1–5 retain their visual content, with limited caption, sizing, and placement changes.

improvement.justification: v2 Table 1 addresses v1's lack of comparisons against external attack methods while retaining the original ablation and defense evidence. Clarified conditioning also improves internal consistency. These gains are limited by unavailable baseline adaptations and relocated natural-trigger material, plus the new FID discrepancy between Tables 1 and 2.
